newsitem.title: CANADA: 150 Quebec youths arrested in holiday riot.
newsitem.headline: 150 Quebec youths arrested in holiday riot.

text.p: Police arrested 150 people in Quebec's two main cities early on Tuesday when youths rioted on the French-speaking province's nationalist holiday.

Some 100 young people were arrested in Quebec City, the provincial capital, and 50 were arrested in Montreal, the largest city. Police said 30 people will be charged on Wednesday with participating in a riot.

A policeman was hurt in Quebec City when police clashed with hundreds of youths who broke shop windows in the sixth consecutive year that young people have rioted there during the annual celebrations. Three teen-agers were also injured. Police said none of the injuries was severe.

In Montreal, youths went on a rampage, breaking shop windows in the city center. The violence erupted on the day of Quebec's patron saint, St. John the Baptist, a date Quebeckers celebrate as their "national" holiday.
"It was a riot. It felt like the youths were worked up. They were looking for a confrontation but we limited the damage," Quebec City police officer Daniel Delisle said.

The trouble began after an outdoor concert attended by about 120,000 people on the Plains of Abraham, a park overlooking the St. Lawrence River where an English expeditionary force defeated French troops to conquer Canada in 1759.

Several hundred youths tried to charge the provincial legislature, where rioters last year smashed windows in a similar rampage. The crowd then moved to the city's old quarter and began throwing rocks and bottles at police.
Riot police used tear gas and a water cannon truck to disperse the crowd. It took them about five hours to clear the streets of the 389-year-old city.

There has been concern in Quebec City that such riots would affect the vital tourist trade, which boosts the local population of 700,000 by three times during the summer. But Quebec Premier Lucien Bouchard said the incidents were isolated and should not jeopardize future celebrations.
"The immense majority of people behaved properly and we just talk about small isolated incidents. It was not a mass phenomenon. There are always marginals in the society," he told reporters.
Quebec City Mayor Jean-Paul L'Allier said he was considering staging only daytime celebrations next year.
